er_0: You wake up in a locked room. There is an old desk, a large painting and a small window.
eo_0: Search the desk|Look behind the painting|Try the window
er_1: In the desk drawer you find a candle and a note: «Light shows the way».
eo_1: Light the candle near the painting|Try the window
er_2: Behind the painting is a small safe with a three-digit lock.
eo_2: Try the code 1-2-3|Go back to the desk
er_3: The window is nailed shut. Outside, it is dark and quiet.
eo_3: Search the desk|Look behind the painting
er_4: In the candlelight, three numbers glow on the painting: 7 – 4 – 1.
eo_4: Open the safe with 7-4-1|Try the window again
er_5: Wrong code. The safe beeps angrily, and nothing happens.
er_6: The safe opens! Inside is an old key and a riddle: «I have a lock but no chest». Where does the key go?
eo_6: The door of the room|The window
er_7: 🎉 The key turns in the door lock with a click — you escaped!
er_8: The key does not fit the window… the candle goes out. Try again!
cs_s_0: At grandma's birthday party, her pearl necklace vanished from the bedroom between 8 and 9 in the evening.
cs_a_0: There were no fireworks to photograph, and the wet footprints came from the garden where Sam said he was.
cs_q_0: I was in the garden the whole evening, taking photos of the fireworks.|I never left the kitchen — the cake needed me every minute.|I only arrived at 9:30, after the fireworks.
cs_c_0: The fireworks were cancelled at 7:30 because of the rain.|Wet footprints lead from the garden door to the bedroom.|The gate camera shows Victor's car arriving at 9:28.
cs_s_1: During the lunch break, the window of the school science lab was smashed.
cs_a_1: The only goal is under the lab window, so Omid was not playing «far from the lab» — and his ball ended up inside.
cs_q_1: I was in the library, reading, for the whole break.|I was playing football in the yard — on the far side, nowhere near the lab.|I was eating in the canteen with my friends.
cs_c_1: A football was found inside the lab, among the broken glass.|The yard has only one goal, right under the lab window.|The librarian saw Mina return a book; Tara’s friends say she sat with them the whole break.
cs_s_2: A chocolate cake disappeared from the office kitchen in the afternoon; only crumbs were left.
cs_a_2: The meeting ended at 2:15, the cake was still there at 2:30 — and the chocolate on his tie gives Mr. Karimi away.
cs_q_2: I was at the dentist all afternoon — my tooth still hurts.|I went out at 2 to buy coffee for everyone and came back at 3:30 — here is the receipt.|I don't even like chocolate, and I was in a meeting until 3.
cs_c_2: The cleaner saw the cake still there at 2:30.|The meeting ended early, at 2:15.|There is a chocolate stain on the manager's tie.
cs_s_3: A small painting disappeared from a museum hall at night, and the alarm never rang.
cs_a_3: Only the guard’s code switches the alarm off, and the camera was turned off from his desk.
cs_q_3: I finished at 10 and went home; the doors were locked behind me.|I walked through every hall every hour and saw nothing.|I was abroad at a conference all week.
cs_c_3: The alarm can only be switched off with the guard’s personal code.|The camera in that hall was turned off from the guard’s desk at 1:00.|The door log shows the cleaner leaving at 10:02, and the director's talk was streamed live from abroad that night.
cs_s_4: The goldfish vanished from its aquarium while the family was out. Three pets are suspected.
cs_a_4: The cat claims it slept on the sofa — but the sofa is covered in wet paw prints.
cs_q_4: Woof! I was barking at the postman in the yard all morning.|Squawk! I can’t swim, and I can’t lift that lid!|Meow. I slept on the sofa all day.
cs_c_4: The aquarium lid was found pushed aside — too heavy for a bird.|There are wet paw prints on the sofa.|The postman says the dog barked at him all morning.
cs_s_5: The answers to tomorrow's exam were copied from the teacher's computer at 5 pm.
cs_a_5: The gym was closed that day, so Babak’s story is false.
cs_q_5: I was at home; my phone was off because the battery died.|At 5 I was at the gym — ask the coach.|I was at the cinema — here is my ticket for the 4 pm film.
cs_c_5: The coach says the gym was closed that day for repairs.|The 4 pm film lasted three hours.|Shirin’s neighbour saw her at home all evening.
cs_s_6: At 10 in the morning someone let the air out of the teacher's bicycle tyres in the school yard.
cs_a_6: The nurse’s office was closed all morning, so Sara could not have been there.
cs_q_6: At 10 I was in the maths exam, in room 12.|I was at the school nurse with a headache.|I arrived at 11 — my bus was late.
cs_c_6: The nurse was ill and her office was closed all morning.|The supervisor confirms Pouya was in the exam until 10:30.|The bus company confirms the bus was 50 minutes late.
cs_s_7: A bicycle with a red basket was stolen from outside the bakery at 7 in the morning.
cs_a_7: The jogger «doesn’t need a bicycle», yet was riding one with a red basket that same morning.
cs_q_7: I ran past at 7, but I don’t need a bicycle — I run everywhere.|I have been baking inside since 5 and never went out.|I slept until 8 — my alarm didn’t ring.
cs_c_7: Later that morning the jogger was seen riding a bicycle with a red basket.|The first customer, at 6:50, says the baker was at the counter.|The student’s roommate says he was snoring until 8.
wa_c_ferdowsi: I was born in Tus, in Khorasan, in the 10th century.|I worked on a single book for about thirty years.|My book tells the stories of the heroes and kings of ancient Iran.|Rostam and Sohrab are characters of my Shahnameh.
wa_c_avicenna: I was born near Bukhara in 980.|I knew the Quran by heart at ten and was treating patients at eighteen.|My Canon of Medicine was taught in European universities for centuries.|Europe calls me Avicenna; Iran celebrates Doctors’ Day on my birthday.
wa_c_rumi: I was born in Balkh in 1207 and lived most of my life in Konya.|Meeting a wandering dervish called Shams changed my life.|My followers are known for their whirling dance.|I wrote the Masnavi, which begins with the song of the reed.
wa_c_cyrus: I lived in the 6th century BC.|I founded the largest empire the world had seen until then.|I allowed the Jews to return from Babylon to Jerusalem.|My cylinder is in the British Museum and my tomb is at Pasargadae.
wa_c_khayyam: I was born in Nishapur in 1048.|I solved cubic equations with geometry.|I helped make a calendar more accurate than the Gregorian one.|My quatrains about wine and the shortness of life are known all over the world.
wa_c_einstein: I worked at a patent office in Bern.|In 1905 I published four papers that changed physics.|I won the Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.|My most famous equation is E = mc².
wa_c_curie: I was born in Warsaw in 1867.|I studied in Paris, where I met my husband Pierre.|I discovered two elements; one is named after my homeland.|I was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, in physics and chemistry.
wa_c_newton: I was born in England in 1642, the year Galileo died.|I built the first practical reflecting telescope.|I invented calculus at the same time as Leibniz.|A falling apple is said to have inspired my law of gravity.
wa_c_davinci: I was born in Italy in 1452.|I drew flying machines centuries before the first plane.|My notebooks are written in mirror writing.|I painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.
wa_c_shakespeare: I was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.|I was an actor and part-owner of the Globe Theatre.|I added hundreds of words to the English language.|I wrote Hamlet and Romeo and Juliet.
wa_c_mozart: I was born in Salzburg in 1756.|I gave concerts all over Europe as a small child.|I wrote more than 600 works and died at 35.|The Magic Flute and Eine kleine Nachtmusik are mine.
wa_c_gandhi: I was born in India in 1869 and studied law in London.|I worked as a lawyer in South Africa for twenty years.|In 1930 I walked 390 km to the sea to make salt.|I led India's struggle for independence without violence.
wa_c_napoleon: I was born on Corsica in 1769.|I became a general at 24.|I crowned myself emperor in 1804.|I lost at Waterloo and died on Saint Helena.
wa_c_cleopatra: I was born in Alexandria in 69 BC.|I spoke many languages — the first of my dynasty to speak Egyptian.|Julius Caesar and Mark Antony were my allies, and more.|I was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt.
wa_c_confucius: I lived in China in the 6th and 5th centuries BC.|I was a teacher with thousands of students.|My students collected my sayings in the Analects.|Do not do to others what you do not want done to you — that is my golden rule.
wa_c_tolstoy: I was born in 1828 on the estate of Yasnaya Polyana.|I fought in the Crimean War.|Late in life I gave away my property and preached non-violence.|I wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina.
wa_c_gagarin: I was born in a village near Smolensk in 1934.|I was a fighter pilot before my most famous job.|My flight on 12 April 1961 lasted 108 minutes.|I was the first human in space.

wa_c_chaplin: I was born in London in 1889.|I was on stage from childhood.|I kept making films without words for years after sound arrived.|My character, the Tramp, wears a bowler hat and carries a cane.
wa_c_edison: I was born in Ohio in 1847.|As a boy I sold newspapers on trains.|I held more than a thousand patents, including the phonograph.|I made the electric light bulb practical.
tp_f_uyuni: The largest salt flat in the world: after rain it turns into a giant mirror where the sky and the ground look the same.
tp_f_pamukkale: White terraces of travertine built by hot springs over thousands of years — its name means «cotton castle».
tp_f_socotra: An island where about a third of the plants grow nowhere else, like the umbrella-shaped dragon’s blood tree.
tp_f_danakil: One of the hottest places on Earth, with yellow and green acid pools, and salt still carried away by camel caravans.
tp_f_zhangjiajie: Thousands of sandstone pillars rise out of the forest; they inspired the floating mountains of the film Avatar.
tp_f_antelope: A narrow canyon in Arizona carved by flash floods, where beams of sunlight fall like spotlights at noon.
tp_f_lut: Satellites measured some of the hottest ground on Earth here — over 70 °C — among giant sand «castles» called kaluts.
tp_f_hormuz: A «rainbow island» of red, yellow and purple soil; the red earth is even used in local cooking.
tp_f_badab: Orange and red terraces made over thousands of years by mineral springs in the mountains of Mazandaran.
tp_f_kandovan: A village where people still live in homes carved into cone-shaped volcanic rocks.
tp_f_cappadocia: Fairy chimneys, underground cities and hundreds of hot-air balloons in the sky at sunrise.
tp_f_petra: A city carved into pink sandstone cliffs more than 2,000 years ago, reached through a narrow gorge.
tp_f_causeway: About 40,000 basalt columns, most of them six-sided, left by an ancient volcanic eruption.
tp_f_plitvice: Sixteen terraced lakes in shades of turquoise, joined by waterfalls.
tp_f_halong: Nearly 2,000 limestone islands rising out of emerald water.
tp_f_hillier: A bubblegum-pink lake right next to the blue ocean, coloured by tiny algae.
tp_f_whitedesert: Chalk rocks shaped by the wind into mushrooms and other strange figures on white sand.
tp_f_bluehole: A round underwater sinkhole about 300 m wide and 125 m deep in the middle of a coral reef.
tp_f_crooked: About 400 pine trees all bent at the base in the same direction — no one knows for sure why.
tp_f_waitomo: Caves whose ceilings glow blue with thousands of tiny glowworms.
tp_f_darvaza: A crater of burning natural gas, on fire since 1971 — nicknamed «the Door to Hell».
tp_f_spotted: In summer its water dries into hundreds of round pools of different colours, full of minerals.
tp_f_meteora: Monasteries on top of huge rock pillars, once reached only by ladders and baskets on ropes.
tp_f_easter: Nearly a thousand giant stone figures, the moai, carved by the Rapa Nui people.

cs_s_8: At a family dinner, Aunt Mahin's new phone disappeared from the living-room table around 9 in the evening.
cs_a_8: The tap was broken, so Darya was not washing dishes — and the phone is buzzing in her pocket.
cs_q_8: I was playing video games in my room with my headphones on.|I only came to return a bowl and left at 8:30.|I was washing the dishes after dinner.
cs_c_8: The kitchen tap was broken that evening — nobody could wash anything.|When someone calls the phone, Darya's jacket pocket starts to buzz.|The neighbour's camera shows the boy leaving at 8:31, and Reza's console was online all evening.
cs_s_9: During the break, someone knocked over the blue paint on the art teacher's desk.
cs_a_9: The blue size-39 footprints match Kian’s shoes, so he was in the classroom after all.
cs_q_9: I wasn’t even in the classroom; I was in the yard.|I was in the library returning books.|I was with the principal, talking about the school trip.
cs_c_9: Fresh blue footprints, size 39, lead from the desk to the door.|Kian wears size 39 — and the soles of his shoes are blue.|The principal confirms Bardia was in her office; the librarian saw Yasmin.
cs_s_10: The zoo's parrot escaped at night. The cage lock was opened with a key, not broken.
cs_a_10: The cage was opened with a key, the vet’s key was at the gate — and the keeper’s car, with a feather in it, left at 11.
cs_q_10: I left at 6 and didn’t come back until the morning.|I locked the cage at 7, as always, and went straight home.|I was taking pictures of the owls on the other side of the zoo.
cs_c_10: The lock was opened with a key; it was not forced.|The gate log shows the vet handing in her key at 6.|A parrot feather was found in the keeper's car, which left the zoo at 11 pm — not at 7.
cs_s_11: The school's football trophy vanished from its glass cabinet on Friday evening.
cs_a_11: Ali says he was home with the flu, yet his photo with the trophy was taken in the school yard that evening.
cs_q_11: I was at a match in another city on Friday.|I locked up at 6 and went home.|I haven’t been to school since Thursday — I had the flu.
cs_c_11: The cabinet key hangs in the janitor’s office, which was locked at 6.|The coach’s match was shown live on TV.|A photo of Ali holding the trophy in the school yard on Friday evening was posted online.
cs_s_12: Two slices of the pizza the class ordered for the teacher's birthday were eaten before she arrived.
cs_a_12: Hana is not allergic to cheese at all — she ate a cheese sandwich yesterday — and her notebook is greasy.
cs_q_12: I don’t eat pizza — I’m allergic to cheese.|I was putting up balloons the whole time.|I was at the door, ready to give the signal when the teacher came.
cs_c_12: There is a greasy fingerprint on Hana’s notebook.|Hana’s friends say she had a cheese sandwich for lunch yesterday.|All of Peyman’s balloons are up, and Shadi did give the signal.
cs_s_13: Grandma's cookie jar was emptied one afternoon.
cs_a_13: The stool was in Sina’s room and his empty homework is full of crumbs.
cs_q_13: I napped from 2 to 4 — ask the cat.|I did my homework all afternoon.|I cleaned the rooms upstairs; I never went into the kitchen.
cs_c_13: The jar is on a high shelf; you need the kitchen stool to reach it.|The stool was found in Sina’s room.|Sina’s homework for today is blank — and there are crumbs between its pages.
cs_s_14: At a wedding, the bride's ring vanished from her table during the dance.
cs_a_14: The cake came out after the dance, and a photo shows the waiter at the bride’s table.
cs_q_14: I was taking photos of the dance the whole time.|I never left my desk — the music never stopped.|I was in the kitchen, bringing out the cake.
cs_c_14: The cake was brought out an hour later, after the dance.|The photographer’s pictures show the DJ at his desk during the whole dance.|One picture shows the waiter beside the bride’s table during the dance.
cs_s_15: In a museum gift shop, an expensive vase was found broken after closing time.
cs_a_15: The till was closed at 4:50, so the cashier wasn’t counting money — and pieces of the vase were in her shoe.
cs_q_15: I was counting the money at the till; I heard the crash from far away.|I was checking the back door.|I left at 5, before closing.
cs_c_15: Pieces of the vase were found in the cashier’s shoe.|The till receipt shows the money was already counted and closed at 4:50.|The door log confirms the guard, and the manager’s bus ticket is stamped 5:10.
wa_c_hafez: I was born in Shiraz in the 14th century.|I knew the Quran by heart, and that gave me my pen name.|Goethe loved my poems and wrote a whole book in answer to them.|People open my Divan to read their fortune; my tomb is in Shiraz.
wa_c_saadi: I was born in Shiraz around 1210 and travelled for about thirty years.|I wrote a book in verse in 1257 and one in prose and verse in 1258.|My lines about the children of Adam being limbs of one body are quoted all over the world.|I wrote the Golestan and the Bustan.
wa_c_razi: I was born in Rey, near today’s Tehran, in the 9th century.|I was the first to describe smallpox and measles as different diseases.|A story says I chose the site of a hospital in Baghdad by hanging meat around the city and seeing where it spoiled slowest.|Iran celebrates Pharmacy Day on my birthday; Europe called me Rhazes.
wa_c_khwarizmi: I worked in the House of Wisdom in Baghdad in the 9th century.|The title of my book on solving equations gave us the word «algebra».|Indian numerals reached Europe through my writings.|The word «algorithm» comes from my name.
wa_c_darius: I became king of Persia in 522 BC.|I built a Royal Road with relay stations from Sardis to Susa.|My inscription at Behistun helped scholars decipher cuneiform.|I began building Persepolis.
wa_c_beethoven: I was born in Bonn in 1770.|I moved to Vienna and studied for a while with Haydn.|I lost my hearing but kept composing.|My Ninth Symphony ends with the Ode to Joy.
wa_c_picasso: I was born in Málaga, Spain, in 1881.|I lived most of my life in France.|With Georges Braque I started Cubism.|I painted Guernica.
wa_c_vangogh: I was born in the Netherlands in 1853.|I sold almost no paintings in my lifetime.|My brother Theo supported me, and our letters are famous.|I painted The Starry Night and the Sunflowers.
wa_c_galileo: I was born in Pisa in 1564.|I improved the telescope and saw the moons of Jupiter.|I was put on trial for saying that the Earth moves around the Sun.|«And yet it moves» is what people say I whispered afterwards.
wa_c_darwin: I was born in England in 1809.|I sailed around the world for five years on HMS Beagle.|The finches of the Galápagos helped me think.|I wrote On the Origin of Species.
wa_c_columbus: I was born in Genoa around 1451.|The king and queen of Spain paid for my voyage.|I sailed west with three ships: the Niña, the Pinta and the Santa María.|In 1492 I reached the Americas, thinking it was Asia.
wa_c_marcopolo: I was born in Venice in 1254.|I travelled to China with my father and my uncle.|I served the great Kublai Khan for years.|My book of travels made Europe dream of Asia.
wa_c_tesla: I was born in 1856 in today’s Croatia.|I worked for Edison for a short time and then became his rival.|I developed motors that run on alternating current.|A car company and a unit of magnetic flux density carry my name.
wa_c_hugo: I was born in Besançon, France, in 1802.|I lived in exile on the island of Guernsey for almost twenty years.|One of my novels made a Paris cathedral and its bell-ringer, Quasimodo, famous.|I wrote Les Misérables.
wa_c_pushkin: I was born in Moscow in 1799.|My great-grandfather was an African brought to the court of Peter the Great.|I died after a duel at 37.|I wrote the novel in verse Eugene Onegin.
wa_c_lincoln: I was born in a log cabin in Kentucky in 1809.|I taught myself law.|I led my country through a civil war.|As the 16th president of the United States, I signed the Emancipation Proclamation.
wa_c_mandela: I was born in South Africa in 1918.|I spent 27 years in prison.|I received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.|I became South Africa’s first Black president.
wa_c_caesar: I was born in Rome in 100 BC.|I conquered Gaul.|I crossed the Rubicon and said «the die is cast».|I was stabbed in the Senate on the Ides of March.
wa_c_verne: I was born in Nantes, France, in 1828.|I wrote adventures full of inventions that did not exist yet.|Captain Nemo is one of my characters.|I wrote Around the World in Eighty Days.
wa_c_nightingale: I was born in Florence in 1820 and was named after the city.|I worked in military hospitals during the Crimean War.|Soldiers called me «the Lady with the Lamp».|I founded modern nursing; Nurses’ Day is on my birthday.
tp_f_naqshejahan: One of the largest city squares in the world, built around 1600 and framed by two mosques, a palace and the bazaar.
tp_f_shushtar: Canals, tunnels and watermills built about 1,700 years ago — a masterpiece of ancient engineering that still works.
tp_n_qeshm: Valley of the Stars, Qeshm, Iran
tp_f_qeshm: Wind and rain carved strange towers here; an old local story says a star fell and turned the ground to stone.
tp_f_masuleh: A village on a steep mountainside where the roofs of the houses are the streets of the houses above.
tp_f_iguazu: About 275 waterfalls along almost 3 km; the biggest is called the Devil’s Throat.
tp_f_victoria: Its spray rises hundreds of metres; the local name means «the smoke that thunders».
tp_f_grandcanyon: A canyon nearly 2 km deep carved by the Colorado River; its rock walls show almost two billion years of Earth’s history.
tp_f_jokulsarlon: A glacier lagoon full of blue icebergs, which wash up on a black sand beach called Diamond Beach.
tp_f_redbeach: A huge marsh covered by a plant that turns bright red every autumn.
tp_f_tianmen: A natural arch high in a cliff, reached by 999 steps and one of the longest cable cars in the world.
tp_f_moraine: Its water is a bright turquoise, coloured by fine rock dust ground by glaciers.
tp_f_marblecaves: Caves of marble on a lake in Patagonia, polished by the waves into swirls of blue and white.
tp_f_deadvlei: Black trees that died centuries ago still stand on a white clay pan among some of the highest red dunes on Earth.
tp_f_santorini: White houses on the rim of a flooded volcano, left by one of the biggest eruptions in human history.
tp_f_machupicchu: An Inca citadel high in the Andes, built of stones fitted without mortar and little known to the wider world until 1911.
tp_f_angkor: The largest religious monument in the world, built in the 12th century and surrounded by a wide moat.
